newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-SLEEPY NORMAN SPARKLES IN SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SLEEPY NORMAN SPARKLES IN SPAIN.

text.p: Australian Greg Norman shrugged off a lack of sleep to produce a spirited opening round in the Spanish Open on Thursday.

Norman, bidding to get back the world ranking number one slot, dropped an early stroke but then ran in two birdies and an eagle to card a three-under-par 69, two behind the surprise early front-runner, English club professional Gary Emerson.
Level with Norman was playing partner Jose Maria Olazabal as the Spaniard continued his remarkable comeback.
Several players were one stroke better on 68 including Argentine Eduardo Romero, Trinidad and Tobago's Stephen Ames, former British amateur champion Iain Pyman of England and Spain's Miguel Jimenez.

Norman, who on Wednesday had a bull dedicated to him by a veteran matador, said after his round: "I only got four hours sleep and I need a minimum of six so I have to be pleased with the opening round.
"When you're younger you could bounce out of bed and go. Now I need to take a couple of painkillers and do some stretching exercises before I can go!"
